items.title: What Hyatt’s CEO Learned by Owning Hotels — and the Trend He’s Most Excited About
items.summary: For most of its history, Hyatt owned its own hotels. Its CEO says that experience never left the company.

items.title: Decoding the New Premium Traveler
items.summary: Every travel company with a premium product is deciding whether the next generation of high-value customers looks like the last one.

items.title: Virgin Atlantic CEO: Don’t Make Customers Pay More for SAF Without the Environmental Benefit
items.summary: Virgin Atlantic CEO Corneel Koster said more progress needs to be made on scaling SAF, which has faced severe supply chain bottlenecks.

items.title: Building Integrated Systems Before the Next Disruption
items.summary: When something goes wrong, every travel company learns what's within and out of its control. Most travel companies can't replicate Qatar Airways’ ownership structure, so the question is how to pinpoint handoff points in their own operation where a failure cascades.

items.title: Revolution’s Steve Case and Certares’ Greg O’Hara Are Betting on Scarce Travel Assets
items.summary: The man who taught America to log on to the internet is going long on the offline world. And the man who is selling Amex GBT in a $6.3 billion deal talks about where he sees his next opportunities.

items.title: Why Banyan Group Talks About ‘Contribution’ — Not ‘Sustainability’
items.summary: Banyan is betting on conservation action rather than beating the sustainability drum. The test is whether contributions to the environment will make a meaningful change, or whether it will just become the newest buzzword.

items.title: Canada’s Alberta Is Courting Gulf Investment — Not Just Gulf Tourists
items.summary: The province is chasing investors to build all-season resorts and ranches its current inventory can't offer.

items.title: Recalibrating Travel: What AI Changes, and What It Doesn’t
items.summary: Every travel operator is weighing where to use AI first: to chase growth or to optimize profitability. The question for any travel company: can you use this economic wave to gain margins, or will you wait for a "normal" economic cycle?
